en.title: Rachael Stirling Drops Intimate Memoir About Iconic Mother Diana Rigg
en.summary: The daughter of the legendary Diana Rigg is set to release a deeply personal memoir. "All About My Mother" promises an honest and moving portrait of the "Avengers" star.
en.body:
The late, great **Diana Rigg** was an actress who commanded attention, whether she was embodying the sharp wit of Emma Peel in **The Avengers** or the formidable Olenna Tyrell in **Game of Thrones**. Now, her daughter, **Rachael Stirling**, is set to offer an intimate glimpse into the life of the woman behind the iconic roles with her upcoming memoir, "All About My Mother". This release promises to be a joyous, funny, and deeply moving tribute, bringing Rigg back to life for the fans who admired her.

Stirling's book delves into the complexities of her mother's life and career. While Rigg herself never penned an autobiography, this memoir serves as a beautiful and honest attempt to capture the essence of the woman she knew and loved. Early descriptions highlight the book as "honest, funny, gossipy, sad and extremely moving," suggesting a candid exploration of Rigg's formidable personality and groundbreaking career. Readers will likely find a portrait of a woman ahead of her time, someone who navigated a male-dominated industry with fierce intelligence and a refusal to be defined by conventional expectations. As the Guardian noted, Rigg's views on marriage and security were refreshingly modern, and her fight for equal pay on "The Avengers" cemented her status not just as a style icon, but as a trailblazer.

## A Daughter's Loving Tribute

"All About My Mother" is more than just a biography; it's a daughter's perspective, offering a unique and personal connection to a global entertainment icon. **Rachael Stirling**, an accomplished actress in her own right, brings a profound understanding of the performance world to her writing. This insider's view, combined with the deep emotional bond of family, is what makes this memoir so eagerly anticipated. It’s a chance for fans to understand the woman beyond the screen, to hear the stories and anecdotes that shaped **Diana Rigg**'s extraordinary life. The book aims to resurrect the woman Stirling knew and loved, making her accessible to a new generation and reminding long-time admirers of her enduring impact.

## For The Devoted Fanbase

For the legions of fans who have followed **Diana Rigg**'s career from her swinging sixties heyday to her later, commanding television roles, "All About My Mother" represents an invaluable addition to her legacy. It’s an opportunity to connect with the star on a more personal level, to understand the triumphs and perhaps the quiet struggles that defined her journey. The book is expected to resonate deeply with those who admired Rigg not just for her talent, but for her strength, independence, and sharp intellect. This memoir is a testament to the enduring power of her performances and the indelible mark she left on film, television, and the broader cultural landscape.

## What's Next

"All About My Mother" by **Rachael Stirling** is scheduled for release on **September 10, 2026**. The 320-page book will be published by John Murray, and is already generating significant buzz among literary and entertainment circles.

content_raw: Beautifully written by her daughter, this is a funny and intimate eulogy to the 60s star of The Avengers who went on to specialise in fierce, complicated women The late actor Diana Rigg declined to call herself a feminist, noting: “Why would I burn my bra? I need my bra.” Nonetheless, her ideas on womanhood were ahead of their time. In an interview with Michael Parkinson, she observed how marriage was “all rather pagan, don’t you think? … A lot of women see it as security. Well, I’m not a woman who yearns for security.” Taking over from Honor Blackman as the high-kicking Emma Peel in the 1960s spy series The Avengers, Rigg refused to play subordinate sidekick to Patrick Macnee’s Steed, turning her character into a beacon of female empowerment. When Rigg learned that not only was Macnee paid significantly more than she was, but the camera operator was too, she demanded a raise. She got it, but that didn’t stop the press from labelling her as a grasping diva. Fifty years later, she told Newsnight: “Equal pay. That’s what feminism means to me, only that.” Continue reading...
